description_en: The Bhaṇḍārībādā stūpa is a village located 1 km to the north of Khalaṅgā (Jumla Bajār), the Jumla district headquarters. The stūpa is built next to a shrine topped by a stūpa (JUM0031) on the edge of a hill ridge to the west of Bhaṇḍārībādā. The two monuments are found in a terrace, next a small road leading to Simkhāḍā, north of Bhaṇḍārībādā.The stūpa is built on a 300 x 300 cm stone base in the shape of amaṇḍala(a square with a central projection - Skt.bhadra-on each side). Above it are five successive steps, also in the shape of a maṇḍala, of decreasing dimensions. On top of the fifth (sixth counting the base) step is theharmikā. It has the same plan as the steps, with one large centralbhadraon each side. Theharmikāis 100 cm high. At mid-height is a horizontal plinth with two registers ofāmalakamotifs. On top of theharmikāare the damaged remains of three steps of decreasing dimensions. These were probably topped by a dome, as it is still visible on the nearby JUM0031.The monument is typologically similar to the stūpa at Kuchi Bihāra (ACH0010, horizontal plinth) and to the one erected on top of the Patharnauli reservoir (DLK0160). Both monuments were built in 1354 CE (ŚS 1276) by Devavarmā, the Great Minister (mahāmātya) of King Pṛthvīmalla. It is therefore likely that this stūpa and the shrine built next to it were both built during the 14th century (Andolfatto 2019, pp. 96-97).The monument is mentioned inSharma 1972, p. 27,Sharma 2012, pp. 188-189 andAndolfatto 2019, pp. 96-97.
